children.text: Design Does* is a co-production between Elisava and the Barcelona Design Museum in collaboration with Domestic Data Streamers. The exhibition collectively explores how design tackles the challenges faced by society, at times offering improvements and, at others, doing just the opposite. Conceived to transcend the limits of space, time and conventional formats, this project explores the responsibility that lies with design and its impact on industry, people, social systems and cultural values. Design Does questions the designer’s role today and in the future as a provider of solutions, humanist, strategist and/or agent of change.

Each year WGSN and Coloro unite the trend forecasting expertise and innovations in the future of color to launch 5 key colors. A Window to the Future of Color is a digital event project for which we worked on 5 animations, and web experience.

For the Milan Design Week 2017 we designed GEA an interactive Marble Machine to visually illustrate the stages of the process of food cultivation and transformation, from farmland to consumer.

Throughout the circuit the marbles animate elements of the landscape and send a different message every time.

This is conveyed digitally through Tweets and physically are delivered to visitors by a thermal printer integrated in the installation.

Since 2006, Unitaid has driven access to health innovations, helping introduce over 150 tools—from HIV medicines to mosquito nets. Marking 20 years, we celebrate partnerships and progress while facing mounting health financing pressures. Innovation means new products and smarter implementation: better delivery, stronger frontline support, and people-centered design. Because access changes lives.

Behind the scenes of the interactive experience we created for Samba TV's CES presentation. The challenge: demonstrate complex cross-platform analytics capabilities in minutes.

The solution emerged from a powerful insight—the connection between attention and intention. Traditional measurement gives fragmented views of audience behavior, but Samba's technology reveals how viewing patterns across devices connect to consumer actions.

We designed visualizations that transformed abstract data capabilities into tangible business answers, allowing executives to explore scenarios directly relevant to their challenges rather than sitting through generic slides.

For the Mobile World Congress in Barcelona, we unveiled a captivating butterfly greenhouse featuring four interactive installations. Leveraging the innovative synergy of TouchDesigner and AI, we crafted an engaging and immersive environment that promises both enjoyment and technological wonder.
Introducing the latest portfolio of Adrià Paituví, a freelance creative producer navigating at the intersection of art, film, music and dance.

children.text: Surely you had never thought that stepping hard or jumping high up could create a unique artistic piece. An audiovisual content where your steps could become light choreographies or your jumps into colorful graphic animations. Yes, with New Balance FuelCell Party it is possible and even you could be the composer of your soundtrack. Treadmills, trampolines and DJ dishes will be part of the spectacular intervention that New Balance will carry out last October 19 in its ephemeral space located in the passage Camps Ellisis, 9. To the purest 'streetsyle' , this new space will be filled with immersive facilities that will transform the movements of each visitor into sounds, colors and lights.

The Guzzo Club is a dynamic space that changes environment between day and night. The Bookcase as a catalyst object of this transformation is working both at rest and by activating different modes. The installation relates projected images with electronic devices that react to the actions of a character that generates an illusion of interaction with objects such as: a disco ball, a fan, oscilloscopes or a tape recorder The different modes that are activated by an app that also controls the LED color. Developed in an 'Open Source' environment, the system allows the integration of new modes and contents.

Combining different kind of technologies, we have created an exhibition to celebrate the 120th anniversary of Roche Italia that take place within the company. The clients are able to interact with several installations to look beyond the present and see the directions of Roche’s research towards innovation in the pharmaceutical field. Scanning their bodies clients can learn about the future of medicine and understand the next steps in the industry.

Jordi Garreta is a creative developer based in Barcelona dedicated to the intersection of code and experience. He designs and builds interactive work that brings technology closer to people, from web interfaces to physical and generative environments.
Currently freelancing and open to both short and long-term collaborations.

Giulia & Vitor's wedding website is a playful and interactive platform designed to celebrate the special day of two close friends. The website provides all the essential wedding information in a fun and engaging way. Guests can contribute to the wedding playlist by adding their favorite songs to a shared Spotify playlist, creating a personalized soundtrack for the celebration. The site also features interactive 3D characters representing Giulia and Vitor, complete with animations that let visitors make them dance. With its joyful design and creative features, the website captures the couple’s unique personalities and adds an extra layer of excitement to their wedding festivities.

Humanity has always sought future perspectives, and today, the urgency to envision a positive future is greater than ever. Enter Habitat 3000, a collaborative virtual reality universe that offers fresh visions of co-created futures. It explores how ecosystems adapt to rapidly changing global conditions, envisions the sounds and appearances of nature, and imagines new alliances. It also delves into the role of technology in this organic world and the aesthetics of the future. Habitat 3000 encourages us to dream and fosters conscious growth, reimagining social and political change. Created by Las Maleantes, it's a virtual reality exhibition featuring interactive ecosystems developed through an open call with artists. This project uses virtual reality as a catalyst for change through gamification and immersion, enhancing the visitor's experience with sound and visual elements. It challenges the prevailing apocalyptic view of the future by showcasing a diverse range of landscapes and creative ideas, ultimately promoting emerging artists experimenting with virtual reality.

Fondazione TOG is an organization for the rehabilitation of children affected by complex neurological disorders. Thanks of the collaboration between TOG and Opendot, we have created an interactive project where sound and body language are used as expressive tools that help children to relate to what surrounds them.

With Makey Makey, the kit to transform anything into a computer keyboard, and Processing, for the audiovisual part, we have designed 3 different sound games based on: sensorial, associative and cognitive stimuli.
Mattdigging

is a music discovery platform built around the personal record collection of a vintage-music curator with two decades of crate-digging experience. It lets listeners explore weekly hand-picked playlists drawn from over 1,500 records, save favorites, and browse selections spanning countries, genres and moods — surfacing hidden gems alongside a constantly growing, richly curated library of sound.
HOLDER OBJECTS

is a Next.js and Shopify-powered e-commerce platform bridging Latin American contemporary and collectible design with European audiences. Built for Berlin-based curators Trinidad Davanzo and Camilo Palma, the site functions as an editorial platform, design store, and cultural archive — showcasing furniture and art-led objects rooted in Latin American heritage, geography, and identity, from Patagonian oak to Mexican volcanic stone.

Christmas 2019 was frosted at the house of Sephora. A powerful machine to produce User Generated Content, surrounded by pillow fights, ice sculptures and other beauty experiences to heat up social media. For the Sephora Frosted Christmas Party 2019 we had created a full interactive system where users could decide which background image they wanted and feel itself as a model for a while.

Collaborated with Immersive Studios to develop an engaging and interactive website that showcases dynamic particle effects, leveraging the power of Three.js and WebGL. The project emphasizes user interactivity through mouse movements and scrolling, creating an immersive experience.

For the contest made by Video Sound Art called Ta Erotika - Hidden Doors, we have created Trans-lucent, an interactive installation based on the stimulation of the imagination in the context of erotism. Light and textile can be an enhancer of our erotic experience, making it more tangible and sensual. The visitor is invited by his movement and dehambulation to modify the perception of the space by playing with the intensity of the light layers. Trans-lucent is composed by lights and translucent textile elements. Textile layers are silently hanging from the celling representing a sexual libido, facing towards a light symbol that empowers and modulates the thought of the player. A rgb led light tube is integrated in the bottom part of each of the tube layers. The RGB Led light tube modify his colour depending of the data produced by a flex sensor located also at the bottom of the fabric.

This project was developed for Hotel Villa Emilia, located in the center of Barcelona, with the goal of connecting the hotel with the surrounding neighborhood and inviting passersby to discover its rooftop space,
La Terrassa

An interactive installation was created at street level, allowing people walking by to trigger visual content as they passed. Using motion detection, the installation responds to pedestrian movement by revealing a curated selection of images and videos showcasing the atmosphere, events, and views from the hotel’s rooftop terrace.

The installation transforms the hotel façade into a dynamic communication surface, turning a simple walk down the street into a playful discovery experience. By blending technology, motion interaction, and audiovisual storytelling, the project invites the public to engage with the hotel in an unexpected and memorable way.

I am Jordi Garreta, a creative developer & technologist based in Barcelona, working worldwide. I’ve dedicated myself to acquiring a comprehensive understanding of creative coding, prototyping, and interactive design.
